title: Cluster 01 DRILL: Photosynthesis
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 5 · 10 questions · 100 marks · 35 parts · one mark per minute, so a little over an hour and a half · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question, and the paper, year and question number are in the Sources block at the foot of each one. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in that same block. If a question cannot be traced to a paper, it is not in here.

Book 5 measured 23% to 25% of the whole A-level on the 9477 specimen, which is the highest of any Book measured. This cluster owns six of its twelve learning outcomes: 3(a) for the chloroplast, 3(b), 3(c), 3(d), 3(e), and the thylakoid half of 3(l).

Explain is 27.7% of structured parts in this Book, nearly double Describe. Photosynthesis is not a describe-the-stages topic in the examiner's hands, whatever the notes look like. Nine of these ten questions ask you to account for something rather than to recite it.

The anchors. Question 6 is 9477 Specimen Paper 2 Question 5, parts (a), (b) and (d), at their real marks and with the specimen's own Figure 5.1. Question 7(a) is Specimen Paper 1 Question 19 word for word, and Question 8(a) is Specimen Paper 1 Question 20 word for word with its own graph. Question 4 is the full-cycle question: the light-dependent stage run end to end for 10 marks, in the wording of a real Section B scheme.

Four real figures. Every one is the actual image from the paper the question came from. Where a figure could not be recovered from a source PDF, the paper's own prose description of it is printed in its place and the part is answerable from that description.

Two MCQs, both from the official specimen. The paper awards one mark for the letter. The drill then asks you to say why each of the other three options fails, which is where the real work is.

Cumulative over Books 1 to 4. Q1(d) needs circular DNA and 70S ribosomes from Book 1 cell structure. Q5(c) needs the hydrophobic core of the bilayer. Q5(d) needs membrane fluidity and temperature. Q7(a) and Q7(b) need active sites and competitive inhibition from Book 1 enzymes. Q8(c) needs kinetic energy and effective collisions. A Book 1 gap surfacing here is worth more than a clean Cluster 1 answer, so say it out loud when it happens.

What the marks reward. Write photolysis, never hydrolysis, because a scheme prints "Reject: hydrolysis" against it. Write ATP is synthesised, never "energy is produced", because two schemes reject that outright. Say stroma, not chloroplast, when a stem prints the word precisely. Name both nouns correctly: the chlorophyll a is photoactivated and the electron is photoexcited. Answer in the singular when a stem says name the structure, because a scheme prints "R! Grana". Quote values with units off any graph you are told to refer to.

The biggest trap in this Book is quoting a number. Total ATP yields, proton-to-ATP ratios and the names of the electron transport chain carriers are excluded in writing by the syllabus. Give the process and the relationship, and quote a figure only where the outcome asks for one.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers and not merely for duplicated labels. Q1 reading a compartment off a real micrograph · Q2 the two spectra and what the gap between them proves · Q3 the light-dependent stage applied to an unfamiliar inhibitor · Q4 the whole of photophosphorylation, end to end, plus what it is for · Q5 how the proton gradient is built, and what happens when the membrane stops holding it · Q6 which Calvin intermediate moves which way, and why · Q7 rubisco as an enzyme rather than as a step in a cycle · Q8 which factor is limiting where, and what a plateau proves · Q9 chloroplast structure argued as efficiency · Q10 three different ways of breaking the same pathway. Two shared marking points exist in the set and both are deliberate. Q4 is the synthesis question, so its list reaches across Q3 and Q5 by design. Q1(c) and Q9 both credit thylakoid folding for surface area, and nothing else on the Q9 list appears anywhere in the set.

Nothing from Books 6 to 9, and nothing from Clusters 2 or 3. Glycolysis, the link reaction, the Krebs cycle, oxidative phosphorylation and the mitochondrion are Cluster 2. Respirometers, hydrogencarbonate indicator, compensation point, chromatography, DCPIP method design and results-table layout are Cluster 3. 9477 Specimen Paper 2 Question 5(c), the mean-rate calculation off Figure 5.1, has been moved to the Cluster 3 drill because it is a data-handling item and Cluster 3 is where data handling is tested.
